map.Lessons 7-1 & 7-2 — part of the Below Ze: Lessons 7-1 & 7-2 are part of the Below Zero arc. integers & opposites · ordering rationals · 6.NOS.C.5–7. Read from start to end. Each gate gives hints and a worked example. It never blocks the page.
map.Episode 1. Same crew, same city — one fo: Episode 1. Same crew, same city. One part of the case. Turn the page when you're ready.
map.The whole grid went dark at 6:14. Jamal: The whole grid went dark at 6:14. Jamal, you and I lead. Get the notebook and evidence.
map.Fact one: Ada Vex built the Pattern Engi: Fact one: Ada Vex built the Pattern Engine where Meridian Avenue crosses Zero Street. Right in the middle.
map.Her street grid IS a coordinate plane. T: Her street grid IS a coordinate plane. The engine is at the origin, (0, 0). Power spreads out from zero, one district at a time.
map.East–west streets count along the x-axis: East–west streets use the x-axis. North–south streets use the y-axis. Where they cross is the origin.
map.Down to −8° tonight. Yesterday's high wa: It drops to −8° tonight. Yesterday's high was 5°. The cellar stays at −3°.
map.Below-zero numbers. Whole ones with no f: Numbers below zero. Whole numbers with no fraction. Integers, right?
map.Correct. Integers: counting numbers, the: Correct. Integers are counting numbers, their opposites, and zero. Opposites are the same distance from zero, on the other side. The heat router wakes when its dial shows the opposite of tonight's reading, −7.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. L: Reader, you're our fifth crew member. Write down the readings and spin the dial!
map.The heat router needs yesterday's log. P: The heat router needs yesterday's log. Pick a reading chip. Then tap its tick on the thermometer: −8°, −3°, and 5°. Next, wake the router. Its dial must show the opposite of −7. Type that number.
map.Conceptual: zero is the freezing mark. N: Conceptual: zero is the freezing mark. Negative readings are BELOW zero. The more negative it is, the LOWER the tick. Opposites are the same distance from zero, on the other side.
map.Procedural: start at 0 and count ticks D: Procedural: start at 0. Count ticks DOWN for a negative reading. −3 is three ticks below zero. For an opposite, keep the distance from zero and switch sides.
map.Heater trucks roll to the coldest distri: Heater trucks go to the coldest district first. But which one IS coldest? One reading is a fraction.
map.Don't trust your eyes. Under a minus sig: Don't trust your eyes. With a minus sign, a big digit means very cold.
map.All four are rational numbers — any numb: All four are rational numbers: numbers you can write as a fraction, like −2.5 or −¾. They look different but share one number line.
map.Rational numbers include integers, fract: Rational numbers include integers, fractions, and decimals, positive or negative. Least means farthest below zero.
map.Sort the ledger, reader — the coldest di: Put the list in order, reader. The coldest district gets the first truck!
map.Four district readings: −2.5°, 0.5°, −3°: Four district readings: −2.5°, 0.5°, −3°, −¾°. Tap the cards in order from least to greatest. Coldest district goes first. Tap a card again to undo it.
map.Conceptual: colder means farther BELOW z: Conceptual: colder means farther BELOW zero. On a number line, the least number is farthest left. With negatives, a bigger digit means colder.
map.Procedural: rewrite everything the same: Procedural: first, write every number the same way. As a decimal, three fourths is 0.75, so −¾ = −0.75. Then go along the number line from left to right.
map.completed Unit 7 · Episode 1: Lights Out: completed Unit 7 · Episode 1: Lights Out in the Below Zero arc, and showed they know integers & opposites · ordering rationals · 6.NOS.C.5–7.
map.Place −6° on a thermometer: start at the: Put −6° on a thermometer. Start at the 0 mark and count six ticks down. That tick is −6.
map.Its opposite keeps the same distance — s: Its opposite is the same distance, six, but on the other side. Six ticks UP lands on 6.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
Write them as decimals: −1.5, 1, −0.5, −2. The one farthest below zero is −2. That's the least.
map.Left to right: −2, −1.5, −0.5, 1. Negati: Left to right: −2, −1.5, −0.5, 1. Negatives can trick you, so check how far below zero each one is.
map.Place all three readings on the thermome: First, put all three readings on the thermometer. Tap a chip, then a tick.
map.A negative reading lives BELOW the zero: A negative reading is BELOW the zero mark. Check which side of 0 your tick is on.
map.−8 is COLDER than −3 — deeper below zero: −8 is COLDER than −3. Farther below zero means a LOWER tick.
map.At least one reading sits on the wrong t: One or more readings are on the wrong tick. Count the ticks from 0 with care.
map.Readings logged, dial at 7 — the heat ro: Readings saved. The dial is at 7. The heat router hums awake!
map.Readings placed! Now the dial: an opposi: Readings placed! Now the dial. An opposite is the same distance from zero, on the other side.
−3 < −2.5 < −¾ < 0.5 — Frostvale first. Heater trucks go out, coldest district first!
map.Careful — −¾ is only ¾ below zero. −2.5: Careful. −¾ is only ¾ below zero. −2.5 is two and a half below. Colder is lower.
map.Not coldest-to-warmest yet. Picture all: Not coldest to warmest yet. Picture all four on a number line, then tap.
